source.title: Highly Scalable Deep Learning Training System with Mixed-Precision: Training ImageNet in Four Minutes
source.authors: Xianyan Jia; Shutao Song; W. He; Yangzihao Wang; Haidong Rong; Fei-Hu Zhou; Liqiang Xie; Zhenyu Guo; Yuan Yang; Li-Wei Yu; Tiegang Chen; Guangxiao Hu; Shao-Huai Shi; Xiaowen Chu

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own 64K-batch ImageNet results and ablations showing that recipe changes can recover test accuracy under a fixed epoch count, qualifying the claim that large batches hurt.
record.gate_note: The paper reports several 64K-batch test-accuracy ablations. Cited results from other teams are not included as rows. It does not report random-label fitting, width sweeps, dropout experiments, or a measured training–test gap.
record.test_reason: The study tests V5's recipe-adaptation clause through its own 64K-batch ImageNet accuracy results and ablations at fixed epoch budgets. It compares against published accuracy baselines, without a controlled smaller-batch run of its own.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that mixed precision, training-recipe changes, and communication optimizations enable 64K-batch ImageNet training without losing baseline accuracy. Their fastest runs achieve 58.7% for AlexNet in 95 epochs and 75.8% for ResNet-50 in 90 epochs.
record.recipe_differences: Uses synchronized SGD with large batches and ImageNet classifiers; adds LARS, mixed precision, weight-decay changes, and batch-normalization changes. It does not compare batch sizes under a fixed epoch budget.
record.method_sensitivity: At batch size 64K, results vary with LARS, weight decay on batch-normalization parameters and bias, and the addition of batch normalization after Pool5. The paper also states that loss scaling is needed at batch size 16K and LARS at 32K for successful mixed-precision training.

fits_no_version.finding: Mixed-precision and single-precision ResNet-50 training achieve similar accuracy: 76.2% and 76.3%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A suitably implemented mixed-precision recipe can preserve full-precision accuracy at 64K batch size.

record.problems: No smaller-batch comparison under a fixed epoch budget is reported in the study's own experiments. The paper reports top-1 test accuracy but not training error or a training–test gap. No uncertainty estimates are stated.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying study results left out. Results attributed to other teams in Tables 4 and 5 and related-work citations were excluded because they are not this study's own results.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under the specified tuning regimes; LARS ablations do not establish this comparison.

A controlled comparison of smaller and larger batches under a common recipe and epoch budget; the workload-dependent batch threshold; longer-training remedies; language models. Accuracy matching uses published reference baselines.
Dropout effects, training-set-size dependence, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, measured generalization gaps, and comparisons with alternative predictors.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples and retraining.

missing.what: The study's own fastest 64K-batch runs: AlexNet achieves 58.7% in 95 epochs on 1024 GPUs; ResNet-50 achieves 75.8% in 90 epochs on 2048 GPUs. These are not other teams' results. They support near-matching or exceeding the published baselines under the adapted recipe; this conclusion comes from the text.
missing.locator: Tables 4 and 5, 'This work' entries; abstract; conclusion

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for the supplied versions. Incomplete recipe recovery does not independently limit V5, which already states that recipe choices matter. Published baselines provide context but do not establish a controlled causal batch-size effect. No uncertainty estimates are reported.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under varying tuning or weight-decay recipes.
No comparison with smaller batches under a fixed epoch budget; language models are not tested. The paper reports 64K-batch image-classifier results and recipe ablations.
Dropout experiments and the effect of removing dropout and weight decay together.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other measures of the training–test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: 64K minibatch training without LARS versus with LARS and mixed precision
rows.locator: Table 1: Effectiveness of using LARS on ResNet-50
rows.note: The table reports the same batch size and epoch count for both conditions.
rows.check: Supports recipe-dependent recovery: 76.2% exceeds the published 75.3% ResNet-50 baseline. The 73.2% comparator is another 64K condition, not a smaller-batch control. Table 1 does not specify enough settings to reconcile its no-LARS accuracy with Table 6's 60.6%.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.locator: Table 6: Effect of LARS to ResNet-50 Training
rows.note: The paper says that even with mixed precision and LARS, this experiment still does not reach baseline accuracy.
rows.check: LARS produces partial recovery from 60.6% to 71.9%, still below the published 75.3% baseline. Both conditions use 64K batches; this does not isolate the effect of batch size.

source_check.locator_found: Section 5.3, Table 6 and Effect of LARS paragraph

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: 64K-batch training with versus without weight decay on batch-normalization parameters
rows.locator: Table 7: Effect of improvements to ResNet-50 Training
rows.note: The paper says this setting combines mixed precision and LARS.
rows.check: Removing BN-parameter decay with mixed precision and LARS restores accuracy from 71.9% to 76.2%, exceeding the published 75.3% baseline.

source_check.locator_found: Section 5.3, Table 7 and Effect of model improvements paragraph

rows.subject: AlexNet
rows.operation_detail: 64K-batch training with versus without regularizing bias, batch-normalization parameters, and the Pool5 batch-normalization addition
rows.locator: Table 8: Effect of improvements to AlexNet Training
rows.note: All three listed strategies are marked ×.
rows.check: This is the all-strategies-off reference condition, not a comparison with itself. Its 55.8% accuracy is below the published 58.8% AlexNet baseline, so an accuracy shortfall is observed. Replace the self-baseline with that reference and describe this as a condition row.

source_check.correct: 55.8% is the all-strategies-off reference result, not a separate comparator. For an accuracy-shortfall comparison, use the published AlexNet baseline of 58.8%.
source_check.locator_found: Table 8, first row; Section 5.1 and Table 3 for the published baseline
source_check.problem: The reference condition is incorrectly represented as a comparison with itself.

rows.check: The value and condition are mismatched. Table 8 assigns 56.4% to no decay on bias alone; 56.3% belongs to no decay on BN alone. Recovery remains incomplete relative to 58.8%.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.note: The text describes the mixed-precision result as similar in accuracy to single precision.
rows.check: The comparison isolates numerical precision at the same batch size. Similar accuracy across precisions does not itself measure a batch-size penalty or its removal; the 76.2% endpoint is already captured by R3.
